_comment: Room Program canon — period-grounded room/building sizing for Structure Generation v2. MEDIEVAL frame: sizes derive from the BAY (the structural module between cross-frames) + house typology, NOT from modern residential area tables. Units = CUBES (1 cube = 1 m). Every value carries a `sources` entry (the grounding rule). 'bays' on a room = how many structural bays it occupies. See docs/structure-generation/StructureBrief.md + docs/structure-generation/StructureGenerationV2.md. Modern 1500/2100 sq ft figures DO NOT apply here.
_units: cubes (metres). bay_length/width in cubes; 'bays' = structural-bay count.

croft.description: Single-room peasant cottage — one 'house' room with a central hearth.
croft.source: Wharram Percy / vernacular cruck cottage; cruck dwelling width <=6 m

sources.width_max: crucks for houses/barns 'no more than 6 m (20 ft) wide' (buildingconservation.com timber-framed buildings)
sources.bay_length: DERIVED ~4 m: 4-bay longhouse 15-18 m / 4 (Wikipedia Longhouse, Germanic 50-60 ft); canonical module per Brunskill, Timber Building in England (1985) — TBD
sources.bays: 1-2 bay peasant cottage (Wharram Percy excavation, Beresford & Hurst)

longhouse.description: Peasant longhouse — dwelling end (inner room + hall) + cross passage + byre, under one roof.
longhouse.source: Dartmoor / Wharram Percy longhouse (Wikipedia Longhouse; English Heritage Wharram Percy)

sources.bays: Dartmoor longhouse = 'two crucked bays, a cross passage, and two crucked bays' (Wikipedia Longhouse)
sources.length: Germanic longhouse '50 to 60 feet long' = 15-18 m (Wikipedia Longhouse)
sources.rooms: inner room (sleeping/dairy) + living room w/ central hearth + cross passage + byre (English Heritage, Wharram Percy)

hall_house.description: Yeoman/gentry hall house — open hall (middle two bays) flanked by service (lower) and solar (upper) ends.

sources.bays: 'four-bay cruck-framed structure, with the open hall taking up the two bays in the middle' (Wikipedia Hall house)
sources.rooms: open hall (middle 2 bays) + service end + solar (Wikipedia Hall house)
sources.example: c.1530 hall house 14.2 m x 6.7 m (Wikipedia Great hall)

manor_hall.description: Stone manor / great hall — large open hall, length 1.5-3x its width and higher than wide.

sources.proportion: 'between one and a half and three times as long as it was wide, and also higher than it was wide' (Wikipedia Great hall)
sources.examples: Stokesay 15.2 x 7.9 m (~1.9x); Winchester 33.8 x 16.8 m (~2.0x) (Wikipedia Great hall)
sources.width_max: largest true cruck span Leigh Court 10.2 m; great halls wider via aisles (buildingconservation.com; Wikipedia Great hall)
